children: Oil trades higher after the U.S. and Iran returned to tit-for-tat strikes, renewing concerns over supply from the Persian Gulf. In early morning European trade, Brent crude oil for November delivery rises 1.35% to $91.73 a barrel, while WTI's most-traded contract rises 1.5% to $87.09 a barrel. American forces struck Iran for the first time in a month earlier this week, prompting Iranian retaliation on Jordan, home to thousands of American troops. "Shipping conditions remain fragile, with another tanker reportedly attacked near Oman" overnight, MUFG's Soojin Kim writes. However, some solace was provided by signs that producers are continuing to export through Hormuz despite the elevated risk, the analyst notes. (josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com)
